subject: Re: Acme - Competitive bakeoff plan and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@acmecorp.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Competitive bakeoff plan and next steps

Hi Sam / Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment before we kick off the bake-off: 

Summary of needs
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support assistant (1k-3k token sessions, heavy context)
- Success criteria: answer accuracy on labeled eval set (>= 90% F1 on intent extraction), 95th pct latency < 400ms, and token cost below $0.003/token equivalent for production throughput.
- Important non-functional: data residency (US), audit logging, and predictable throughput for peak hours.

Proposed competitive bake-off plan (attached: acme_bakeoff_testplan.xlsx)
1) Sanity passes (by end of next week) — model pairings: Redwood-curated open LLM vs Hyperscaler-managed LLM (Azure/GCP). Smoke on 100 eval examples. Owner: Aditya.
2) Performance + latency run (week of Mar 30) — 10k synthetic sessions, measure p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost. Owner: Redwood infra (Aditya) + Acme tech (Jordan).
3) Quality evaluation (week of Apr 6) — full labeled eval (10k), automated metrics + human review of failure modes. Owner: Acme data + Redwood PM.
4) Canary integration (mid-Apr) — run behind feature flag on 5% traffic and monitor errors and user metrics. Owner: Acme engineering.

Differentiators we plan to highlight vs hyperscalers:
- Predictable per-token economics with intelligent batching/caching to reduce cost for repeated context
- Dedicated inference variants for consistent latency (can reserve capacity)
- Built-in rollouts and fallbacks to keep production available during model updates

Ask / next items from you
- Confirm stakeholders and procurement contacts (please confirm procurement@acmecorp if correct)
- Approve the proposed timeline or suggest date constraints
- Share a representative eval dataset (or samples) we can use for the sanity pass

I attached a draft test plan and a short comparison doc with our suggested test cases.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff next Tue (Mar 23) to lock test owners and cutover windows.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sam Patel <s.patel@acmecorp.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Competitive bakeoff plan and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications: 

- Procurement: yes, procurement@acmecorp.com is correct; I’m looping them in on the thread.
- Pricing comparison vs hyperscalers: can you include a cost-per-1000-tokens and expected monthly run-rate for our projected 50M tokens/month? We need the hyperscaler comparison side-by-side.
- Test dataset: I’ll upload a 500-sample subset of our labeled conversations to the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow.

Also, can we get explicit success thresholds for throughput (TPS) and CPU/GPU footprint expectations so our infra team can pre-approve resource allocation?

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Corp
s.patel@acmecorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0110

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700

On Wed, Mar 18, 2026 at 10:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment before we kick off the bake-off:

Thanks team — putting some of the technical commitments here so they’re explicit for the bake-off: 

Technical plan highlights:
- Test vectors: Sanity (500 samples), Full eval (10k labeled), Stress (10k synthetic sessions over 1 hour).
- Latency targets we propose to validate: p95 < 400ms (single-request, 1k tokens), p99 < 700ms. We recommend a dedicated pool for the performance runs to get stable numbers.
- Cost calc: we’ll provide a simplified cost model (attached: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-comparison.pdf) showing throughput-adjusted token cost and expected monthly spend at 50M tokens.
- Data controls: logs will be stored in your US-only bucket; audit trail available for each request (request_id, model_version, route).

Owners and timeline (draft)
- Sanity pass (Aditya) — complete by 2026-03-26
- Performance run (Aditya + Jordan) — 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-02
- Quality eval (Acme data team + Redwood) — 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-09
- Canary (Acme infra) — target start 2026-04-15

I’ll attach the comparison and a lightweight Jupyter notebook for running the smoke tests. Let me know if you want us to run the perf harness ourselves or hand over the test harness for your infra to run.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - Competitive bakeoff plan and next steps

Looping in a couple high-level asks from my side: 

- SLA/throughput: we should confirm target tail latency and throughput per region. If Acme needs sub-350ms p95 at peak we should discuss Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to avoid noisy-neighbor variance.
- Cost guardrails: we can set budget alerts and automated fallback to a more cost-efficient model variant if spend hits thresholds during the canary. Recommend we capture the thresholds now.
- Commercial: I’ll work with finance to draft a provisional pricing sheet for the dedicated option if we hit the performance targets.

Please make sure procurement has the draft SOW and timeline for approvals so we don’t get blocked in April.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and owners below (finalized plan attached):

- Sanity pass (500 samples): Owner: Aditya; Due: 2026-03-26
- Perf run (10k synthetic sessions): Owner: Aditya + Jordan; Run window: 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-02
- Quality eval (10k labeled): Owner: Acme data team + Redwood; Window: 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-09
- Canary (5% traffic): Owner: Acme infra; Target start: 2026-04-15
- Commercial pre-approval for Dedicated capacity if needed: Owner: Vivek + Acme procurement; Target: 2026-04-10

Acceptance criteria (as discussed):
- Quality: >= 90% on labeled eval metrics or agreed list of critical intent accuracies
- Reliability: p95 < 400ms in perf run; canary must show stable error rates and <1% increase in user-facing errors
- Cost: projected monthly cost at 50M tokens must be within the budget band Sam shares (please post the budget number to this thread).

Kickoff: I scheduled a 30-minute kickoff for Tue Mar 23, 09:00 PT. Please accept the calendar invite; we’ll use that meeting to lock owners and finalize the test harness handoff.

If procurement needs the SOW earlier I can send the draft now.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
